HOBAN Recruitment has partnered with a leader in the NDIS Support Disability space.      Working for an organisation that offers compassionate and personalised care to individuals with diverse needs and our dedicated teams provide a range of support services, including NDIS Support Coordination, Psychosocial Recovery Coaching and Allied Health. We strive to empower individuals to lead fulfilling lives and promote inclusivity and accessibility in the community.     The Role       As a  Support Coordinator  you will join the  Campbelltown  team on a permanent full-time basis. The purpose of this role is to work under the Senior Support Coordinator in the company to assist NDIS participants in the coordination of their supports funded in the NDIS plans. The goal is to ensure that participants can achieve their expected goals including of independence and well-being so that they are better able to participate in community.     Main responsibilities include:    
 
 Doing admin work to Coordinate the day-to-day operation of the NDIS Support Coordination Services 
 Contribute towards participant assessment care planning, response to referrals and reviews in line with MDSS'S Policies and procedures. 
 In collaboration develop and promote a team-based approach to deliver participant centered care and services 
 Collaborate with participants, fostering an understanding of their needs and aspirations to explore options and develop actions that best meets their care needs. 
 Gathering data, booking appointments, supports and services 
 
    What you need    
 
 Minimum 6 months to 1 year experience as a Disability Support Coordinator or similar role in disability - knowing the basics. 
 Qualification or enrolled in a course for Disability Services, Aged Care or other relevant Community Services 
 Experience working with NDIS participants with knowledge of NDIS Operational Guidelines 
 Highly developed communication and interpersonal skills 
 Team player who is driven by compassion and role purpose 
 An Australian driver's license, Working with Children Check, National Police Clearance, First Aid Certificate and a NDIS Workers Screening Check 
 Own vehicle and comprehensive car insurance 
 Excellent admin, office and PC skills. 
 Passion to grow to become a Support Coordinator 
 Care Coordinators encouraged to apply 
 
      Benefits    
 
 Flexible start and finish times 
 Lunch provided once a week 
 Access fleet vehicles 
 Parking and expenses paid 
 Monthly employee activities 
 True career progression, take your career where you want it to go!! 
 
   Apply now to start your journey with a leading NDIS Provider!

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     HammondCare Waratah is currently looking for a Weekend Cook-Chef to join our team.

HammondCare has a unique model of care which places the resident's needs as our number one priority.

As a part of the Support Service's Team, you will support our model of care by delivering high quality meals within the MAIN KITCHEN at our Waratah Facility catering for our 232 residents in accordance with the organisational mission and mission in action statement.

Core Responsibilities:

Reporting to the Support Services Manager you will be responsible for;

Preparing nourishing, appetising, and culturally appropriate meals that meet individual dietary needs and preferences. This includes ensuring meals are visually appealing and served at the correct portion size and temperature.

Ensuring strict adherence to the Food Safety Program (FSP), HACCP standards, and all relevant health and safety regulations. This also involves complying with the Aged Care Quality Standards, specifically Standard 6: Food and nutrition.

Preparing residents' specific dietary requirements, including texture-modified food for those with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia).

Responding to feedback and addressing concerns promptly.

Maintaining accurate documentation related to food safety, resident dietary needs, and operational data.

To be successful in this role, you will:

Be flexible and able to commit to a range of shifts including weekends.

Value teamwork but also be able to work independently and show initiative.

Must have experience in cooking for large numbers in a commercial kitchen and or an aged care environment.

Have an understanding of The vulnerable persons guidelines for food safety or willingness to learn and incorporate these into your everyday work routine.

Demonstrated understanding of safe manual handling practices.

Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Experience in preparing and cooking bulk meals.

What are the benefits of working with HammondCare?

Flexible working environment to deliver a healthy work-life balance.

Gain access to multiple health and fitness facilities at a low fee with Fitness Passport

Be supported & empowered in your role to really make a difference to our residents.

A workplace trainer on each site committed to your ongoing training & development.

Access to not-for-profit salary sacrificing arrangements.

Shift times.

0630-1500

0900-1730

About HammondCare:

HammondCare is an independent Christian charity that has been serving families in Australia since 1932. We are an organisation that is led by our values, our passion is improving the quality of care for people in need.

As one of Australia's most innovative health & aged care providers, we champion life for every person in our care.

Does this sound like you? Apply Now!

For more information, please contact Sarah Egan - segan@hammond.com.au

HammondCare is committed to creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity and inclusion. We strive on creating an equal employment environment where everyone from any background can be themselves.

All short-listed applicants for these positions will be asked to consent to a criminal record check, pre-employment medical assessment & complete a NDIS Worker's Screening check.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     At Estia Health, we're more than just a workplace: we're a community dedicated to enriching lives and making a difference. If you're passionate about aged care and want to be part of something meaningful, then we want to hear from you.

Everyday, over 14,000 employees choose to make a difference at Estia Health, sharing a joint purpose to enrich and celebrate the lives of our residents. With 96 homes (and growing), across Queensland, New South Wales, South Australia and Victoria, you will play a part in positively impacting the lives of our residents and their families.

Join us in playing a special role in the future of aged care.

Estia Health Hamilton requires an experienced Rostering Administrator to join the team. This is a full time position Monday to Friday 7am to 3pm.

Working alongside the Residential Manager you will be a vital member of the Administration team for our home.

About the Role

You'll be hugely important in making sure our home runs smoothly - an indispensable helper to our residential aged care manager and client services officer.

Usually, your day will involve:

Friendly customer service to everyone - whether in person, on the phone or over email

Rostering ensuring all shifts are covered to provide care for our residents

Keeping on top of paperwork - record keeping, filing etc

Supporting the office manager and residential aged care manager in their daily tasks

You'll be a people person and problem-solver, with high attention to detail. You'll also have:

A real desire to make a difference in people's lives

Strong interpersonal and communication skills, both verbal and written

A proactive attitude and ability to work in a fast-paced environment

Solid computer and data skills

Previous experience in a reception-administration position (highly regarded)

Benefits available:

Retail savings with the Blue Light Card

Discounted car hire

Employee Assistance Program for you and your family

Free Wellbeing App to support your mental and physical health

Novated leasing for vehicles

Workplace banking support

ACN membership discounts for nurses

Discounted health insurance with nib health

Discounted JB HiFi

As one of the largest and fastest growing aged care providers in Australia, we need exceptional people to join us on our journey of providing high quality person centred aged care and services. If this is you, Apply now!

Estia Health is committed to embracing diversity, equity and inclusion in our workplaces. We encourage applications from people of all ages, cultures (including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples), abilities, sexual orientation and gender identities. If you need assistance to participate in our application process, please let us know.

Please be advised that we do not accept emailed applications for this position. To apply, simply click the 'Apply' button and follow the instructions provided.

Note: All shortlisted applicants will need to pass the required background checks. During the influenza season, all staff are required to provide evidence of a current influenza vaccination. If you are interested in a role, please ensure you apply online, as we do not accept emailed resumes.    Click here to Apply now →

Make an Impact: Senior Speech Pathology Position in Laryngeal Disorders

As the Senior Speech Pathologist - Laryngeal Disorders, you'll utilize highly specialized skills to manage complex patients with laryngeal disorders, using techniques like videofluoroscopy and FEES in a new Speech Pathology Led service. 

About the role: 

Reporting to the Manager of Speech Pathology Acute Services, some of your duties as the Senior Speech Pathologist may involve:

Providing leadership, supervision and consultancy services related to laryngeal disorders. 

Collaborating with the Advanced Practitioner Speech Pathologist and ENT to evaluate a new Speech Pathology led service for outpatients with laryngeal-based disorders.

Actively pursuing opportunities as required to maintain currency of clinical knowledge in the area of adult disorders of swallowing and communication.

About you:

Appropriate degree in Speech Pathology or equivalent qualification which gives eligibility for full membership of the Speech Pathology Association of Australia.

Extensive clinical experience in the acute management of adult communication and swallowing disorders demonstrating expertise in the assessment and management of laryngeal based disorders including laryngeal hypersensitivity syndrome, dysphonia and dysphagia, including the use of VFSS and FEES

Demonstrated experience in training and clinical supervision of speech pathology staff, students or allied health assistants

Experience in clinical protocol-procedure-pathway development

Experience in collecting, analysing and interpreting data, and making appropriate recommendations

Tweed Heads Region, NSW, Full Time, Admin/Office
Vacancy Listing Dates 28/07/2026 to 25/08/2026
Please Quote Reference Number 17841
- Skilled Office Manager required
- Full time role
- Join the Victory Auto World team in Tweed Heads

About Us

Victory Auto World is a premier automotive dealership dedicated to delivering exceptional customer service and top-tier vehicles to our community. To support our ongoing growth and ensure the seamless execution of our daily dealership operations, we are seeking a highly organised and proactive full-time Office Manager to join our leadership team.

Position Overview

As the Office Manager at Victory Auto World, you will be responsible for orchestrating, organising, and controlling the complete functions, administrative infrastructure, and personnel resources of our dealership’s administrative office. You will work closely with dealership executives, department heads (Sales, Service, and Parts), and administrative staff to ensure maximum efficiency, absolute regulatory compliance, and a smooth workflow across the business.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:
- Contribute to the strategic planning and operational review of dealership administrative services; establish daily office priorities, and set rigorous performance and service standards for clerical operations.
- Manage and allocate human resources, workspace, and physical office equipment to ensure the administrative department supports the fast-paced sales and service environments.
- Assign daily workloads to clerical and administrative staff, actively monitor work performance, and coordinate core personnel activities including hiring, training, performance management, and payroll processing.
- Systematically manage the office's data systems, accounts, and dealership records, ensuring accurate tracking of administrative overheads and internal documentation.
- Liaise closely with qualified professionals (including corporate accountants, legal advisors, and Ford brand representatives) to coordinate broader dealership business and facilitate swift resolution of operational problems.
- Ensure all office equipment, digital operating networks, and physical administrative spaces are meticulously maintained and stocked.
- Ensure all workplace practices strictly comply with relevant Australian government legislation, privacy policies, corporate procedures, and automotive industry protocols.
- Oversee and enforce full compliance with occupational health and safety (WHS/OH&S) regulations within the administration facilities to guarantee a safe working environment.

Skills, Qualifications, and Experience Required:
- An Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) Diploma or higher qualification in Business Administration, Management, or a closely related field, or an equivalent overseas qualification.
- Alternatively, where no formal qualification is held, at least three (3) years of relevant professional experience may substitute for the qualification, consistent with the ANZSCO Skill Level requirements.
- Where the applicant holds the relevant qualification, at least one (1) year of relevant full-time work experience (or equivalent part-time experience) is required to meet the Subclass 482 visa requirements.
- Proven experience working as an Office Manager or in a senior administrative leadership capacity, ideally within the automotive or dealership sector.
- Advanced proficiency in office management software, dealer management systems (DMS), Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook), and payroll structures.
- Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with a proven ability to manage office personnel and liaise effectively with external professionals.
- Strong critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and a detailed understanding of Australian workplace compliance standards.

A salary of $80,000 - $95,000 per annum (plus superannuation) will be offered to the successful candidate.

How to Apply

If you possess the required skills and experience to thrive in this pivotal role, please submit your current resume and a cover letter detailing your suitability.

Apply now through our online application form -
https://www.netyourjob.com.au/jobs/17841.php
